question.knowledge_point: Finding Two Scalar Factors in a Linear Combination
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/fc7d37da99173b7fa99f2f5f0bbf1478a54505628ed827488a18b3d01535f81f.png)

Consider the picture above. Given that $l=\lambda j+\mu k$, find $\lambda $ and $\mu .$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14073957/assets/6c9273c0b89d4c06c8a8591b8e8e94b0c83b2d1d4bd04b64ed8cb0a185619b5f.png)

In $△OJL$ shown above, we have 

- $OJ=|j|$

- $\overset{\to }{OJ}$ has the opposite direction to $j$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{OJ}=-j.$

Similarly:

- $JL=2|k|$

- $\overset{\to }{JL}$ has the opposite direction to $k$

Hence, $\overset{\to }{JL}=-2k.$

Additionally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}l & =\overset{\to }{OJ}+\overset{\to }{JL} \\  & =-j-2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, $l=\lambda j+\mu k=-j-2k.$

Since $j∦k,$ the linear combination can only be written in one way. Equating the coefficients, we get:

- $\lambda =-1$ and $\mu =-2$
